transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Morales (Ventana Head of MLOps), Owen Price (Ventana NLP Eng), Samira Khan (Ventana PM)
Links shared: guardrail-tuning-v3.docx, prompt-set-v12.csv, scoring-spreadsheet-v4.xlsx, benchmark-plan.md

Summary: quick sync to review last week's regression spike, go over prompt set changes and scoring thresholds, align on action items for next focused batch and schedule dedicated latency run. Customer raised a few new failure modes and asked about fallback strategies and private deployment latency expectations.

Topics: regression spike root causes, false positive vs false negative tradeoffs, guardrail trimming, prompt set pruning, scoring threshold adjustments, canary vs full rollout, Dedicated latency benchmark, SOC2/audit ask reminder.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. we shortened this to 40-ish minutes for a quick triage. Ravi and I will run through the regression artifacts, then hand to Ventana for the flagged cases.
[00:18] Ravi: hi, uh, quick context — last week we saw a 3.7% drop in the pass rate on the safety score for the billing intent prompts after prompt-set v11 went live. we rolled a soft fix overnight but wanted to align on next steps.
[00:36] Lena: yeah, thanks. that drop showed up mostly in the "confident-non-answer" bucket — model produced answers that were allowed but mismatched intent. some were format issues and some were hallucinations.
[00:50] Owen: to add, about 60% of those failures are in longer-dialog prompts where the prefix caching seems to be truncating earlier context, so scoring gets confused. not sure if it's our prompt shaping or runtime kv cache.
[01:06] Ravi: interesting — could be both. on our side we made a change to the prefix trimming heuristic to reduce token cost which might lose a heuristic signal. i can instrument a run that preserves the last 512 tokens and compare.
[01:22] Samira: our metric is pretty black-and-white right now: pass if top-1 label matches intent and guardrail==false. we want to reduce false positives (safe responses flagged) because ops is drowning, but we can't miss unsafe ones.
[01:40] Maya: exactly — tradeoff. so today's goal: pick threshold tweaks to head off the false positives and produce a prioritized list of 20 failure cases you want fixed first.
[01:52] Lena: sounds good. quick Q: can you remind us what the current scoring threshold is? i thought it slid to 0.65 after the last update.
[01:59] Ravi: correct — overall safety confidence threshold is 0.65, but we have route-specific overrides: e.g., billing-route has hard reject at 0.7. the regression highlighted that override interaction.
[02:15] Owen: that's the weird bit — when the override exists sometimes the composite score is computed differently, the aggregator pipeline does a max rather than a weighted average. might be contributing.
[02:28] Ravi: hmm, good catch. i can check the aggregator code path. may be an unintended rope of logic.
[02:33] (background: someone typing)
[02:40] Maya: ok, walkthrough — Ravi, can you show the histogram you mentioned?
[02:45] Ravi: sure, pulling up the dashboard. i see a peak of low-confidence answers between 0.4 and 0.6 for billing intents on the v11 run, whereas v10 had a more centered distribution around 0.75. so the model change plus trimmed prefix likely shifted probability mass.
[03:08] Lena: is that a model change or prompt change? we didn't change the core model, just prompt variants.
[03:14] Ravi: prompt-set tweaking is the proximate cause; we increased brevity and removed some guidance tokens to save cost. that made the model less anchored on the schema.
[03:25] Owen: aha — so cost saving tweak induced drift. we need to balance. can we A/B the prompts, keep the old guidance for longer dialogues?
[03:33] Maya: yes — canarying is easy with Redwood Dedicated. we can route 10% to a canary that keeps the old prompt plus extra context. that'll give you a direct comparison.
[03:45] Samira: are there latency impacts with the old prompts? because we have hard latency SLO 350ms tail at 95%.
[03:52] Ravi: small increase due to extra tokens in the prompt; we're still within 350ms on hosted but Dedicated profiling could differ. that's why we proposed the dedicated latency benchmark next week.
[04:04] Lena: ok. about guardrails — a few of the false positives were from our sanitization rules misfiring: the regex strip removed a token and changed intent.
[04:14] Owen: and one case was where the model answered a legal question with a confident-sounding statement — flagged as unsafe by the legal guardrail, but our ops flagged it as false positive since it's allowed under policy. so mismatch between policy and guardrail definition.
[04:28] Maya: that's actually a policy alignment issue. Samira, can you confirm legal's allowed list?
[04:33] Samira: yes, we'll confirm. we want a tighter definition but also avoid overblocking product flows. i'll coordinate and send a clarified bullets doc.
[04:42] Lena: good. second ask — can Redwood provide a small scoring debug dump with token-level attribution so we can see which tokens drove the safety score?
[04:52] Ravi: yes, we have a debug option that emits per-token logits and attention weight approximations. it's a bigger payload but useful for root cause. we'll include for the 1k batch.
[05:03] Owen: great. can you also include the kv-cache lengths per request? might help confirm the prefix trimming hypothesis.
[05:09] Ravi: yes added.
[05:12] (pause)
[05:20] Maya: ok, let's walk the priority list you sent last Friday — there were five clusters: format, hallucination, intent-mismatch for long dialogs, sanction-check false flags, and math/units errors. want to triage each quickly and agree what to flip.
[05:34] Owen: format — we can hard-format the billing response with templates so small variations won't fail. that reduces NLU burden.
[05:41] Lena: hallucination cluster — seems model-produced invented account numbers, that's bad. we need a strict no-personal-data fallback where it responds with "i don't know" and escalates.
[05:52] Samira: agreed — a conservative fallback for PII should be enabled immediately.
[05:56] Ravi: we can add a guardrail that returns a canned escalation when PII-score exceeds 0.6. we'll test for false positives though.
[06:05] Maya: on the math/units items — v11 reduced numerical prompt guidance which made the model less precise. we should put math-heavy prompts back to a specialized prompt that includes working steps.
[06:16] Owen: yes. i'll flag the 30 prompts that need that.
[06:20] Maya: perfect.
[06:22] (timestamp jumps to 10:05)
[10:05] Ravi: quick note, we also saw a small uptick in token consumption when the model tried to be verbose to compensate; might increase cost. we'll quantify delta in the batch.
[10:15] Lena: cost is one thing, but reliability is priority. tell us the minimal change to restore pass rate to baseline.
[10:22] Ravi: minimal change is reintroduce the guidance anchor for long dialogs and raise billing-route threshold from 0.7 to 0.72; that should push the pass rate back ~2.8 percentage points in our sim.
[10:34] Samira: raise to 0.72? ok but we need to see false negative impact.
[10:38] Ravi: yes, that's why the 1k batch with debug payload is critical.
[10:43] Owen: about fallback strategies — if the model fails safety, can we route to a lower-capacity deterministic reranker or a rules engine?
[10:51] Maya: yes, Redwood supports a fallback chain: primary model -> lightweight reranker (low cost) -> canned response/escalation. can configure per-route.
[10:59] Lena: do you have any example of latency impact for a full fallback chain?
[11:04] Maya: typical additional latency for a rerank step is 40-60ms, for a full model fallback depends on model size, but the routing layer can call a smaller quantized candidate which keeps it under 100ms additional for most cases.
[11:15] Owen: that's acceptable if it reduces incidents.
[11:18] Samira: also from compliance: we need audit logs of any fallback events for legal review. is that captured?
[11:24] Ravi: yes, every decision (score, guardrail flag, reroute) is logged and can be exported to your SIEM. we can show a sample log format in the next email.
[11:33] Lena: excellent. does that include KMS key id for encrypted-at-rest payloads?
[11:38] Ravi: yes, we log key fingerprints and can provide HSM/KMS integration details; that's in the private deployment docs.
[11:45] Maya: ok — new item — Samira you mentioned a stakeholder review on roll-forward. what's your internal timeline?
[11:50] Samira: we have an ops review on 11/12 and an exec review on 11/18. ideally we want the pilot stable by 11/10 to present metrics.
[11:59] Maya: timeline aligned. we've got two milestones: 1) quick regression mitigation by 11/06, 2) dedicated latency benchmark by 11/09, then ops review.
[12:10] (typing)
[12:18] Owen: question — any concerns about private deployment vs hosted? execs lean to Private for data residency but that adds setup time.
[12:27] Maya: Private deployments have extra lead time but give you VPC, audit controls. however the immediate canary routing and guardrail tuning can happen on hosted while you parallelize Private setup.
[12:36] Lena: ok we'll prioritize tuning now then decide after the ops review.
[12:40] Ravi: for the 1k run i'll include two variants: old-guidance prompt and new-brief prompt, each instrumented with per-token logits, kv-cache length, and guardrail debug. i'll also run the aggregator both as weighted-average and max to reproduce the difference.
[12:56] Samira: perfect. also can you tag the cases where the reranker would have changed top-1? we want to know how often reranker helps.
[13:05] Ravi: yes will produce a column for reranker-top1 delta.
[13:10] (short silence)
[13:18] Maya: okay quick admin — i will drop the guardrail tuning doc in the shared drive and ping everyone. it contains suggested scoring thresholds and a rollback playbook.
[13:28] Maya: also note: we recommend a staged rollout: 10% canary for 48 hours, if no uptick in safety fail, go to 40% then full.
[13:39] Lena: what's your recommended alert threshold for rollback?
[13:44] Ravi: we suggest a 1% absolute pass-rate drop or any single-day spike of >250 failed transactions for high-severity categories.
[13:54] Owen: that seems sensible.
[13:56] Samira: one more thing — legal asked for a short note on how model updates are versioned and how to revert. do you have a quick summary?
[14:03] Maya: yes, model + prompt sets + runtime config are all versioned. we keep immutable artifacts per deploy and have automated rollback that can be triggered via API or console with a canary-prevent flag. i'll include a one-pager.
[14:14] Lena: nice.
[14:17] (timestamp jump to 20:05)
[20:05] Ravi: small risk note: when you enable per-route hard thresholds it can cause cascading rejections if downstream routing defaults to a stricter aggregator. we'll highlight that in the debug output.
[20:18] Owen: understood.
[20:22] Maya: ok circling to next steps — we agreed Ravi runs the batch, returns CSV + debug by 11/06. Ventana to upload edge-case set by 11/05. Maya to share docs today. schedule benchmark for 11/09.
[20:36] Samira: all good. any blockers?
[20:39] Lena: nothing blocking; just resource time to label the 20 cases.
[20:43] Owen: i'll carve out time.
[20:46] Maya: great. final quick Q from me — do you want Redwood to try a lightweight prompt engineering workshop? could be 60-90 minutes to iterate with your NLP team.
[20:57] Samira: yes please. a hands-on session would be great, maybe 11/04 or 11/05 morning PST.
[21:04] Maya: i'll send a poll.
[21:07] (wrap up)
[21:15] Maya: thanks everyone — recap and notes in the shared doc, action items listed. we'll follow up in email with the files.
[21:22] Lena: thanks, bye.
[21:25] Owen: bye.
[21:27] Samira: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on quality: transcription picks up filler words and sometimes misattributes fast talk — expect minor name swaps in places; timestamps are approximate.
